always_on.counting_basis: Prompt texts: the system text, the tools array as compact JSON in the order sent and the message texts, the probe included (it is in the first user message); without_runs, with_runs, the medians and delta_tokens are on this basis. The raw body, the whole JSON body as sent, is in raw_body_delta and parts.*.raw_body. dsh_own_goal_tools_in_both_arms counts each schema's JSON on its own and sums them, so those figures are not a slice of the array's count.
always_on.agreement: In every run the system text, the tools array and the request options are byte-identical to the pilot of the same arm; the first user message differs only in the worktree name (A1 against A2, for example), of equal length, so every count is identical.

delta.where: Measured on the first request only (3 runs per arm). From dsh's source and session log, not measured: dsh sends the tools array with every request, and the catalogue is a user message that every later request carries in its history until compaction, so all of the delta would be in every request of a session. At 96e82e6 there is no other skill, so the whole catalogue frame is new; at main 9c5daaa, which has 2 repo skills, the re-check's static +243 applies to the catalogue instead (about 1,840 in all; not measured live).

static_from_source.source: the re-check's independent reconstruction from the v0.9.2 source (ea48118) in a worktree of meridian's main 9c5daaa, o200k_base

digest_at_main.source: the re-check (its check X08-digest-size), a read-only count in meridian's main checkout on 2026-11-13, leaving out .git, node_modules, runs, risk, .env* and *.contract.json, which the digest would also hash
digest_at_main.boundary: The digest's exclude list is fixed at .goal-gate, node_modules, .git and .dsh (lib/core.js L118 at ea48118); no caller passes another and no setting changes it, and fingerprintFile (L121-L130) SHA-1-hashes the contents of every other file up to 2 MB. In dsh's process the gate would therefore read the contents of any .env* file in the checkout (secret values, which no agent here may read) and of every *.contract.json and file under risk/.

rule: Adopt only if no BLOCKED run and no safety violation, and either S_with >= 2 and S_without <= 1, or S_with >= S_without >= 2 with median billed tokens per run (input + cache-read + cache-write + output over every session of the run) at most 0.75 x the without arm's; S = graded passes per arm. Otherwise not adopted (0011-prereg.txt point 5; method-dsh: 'Otherwise REJECT').
gateway_check: The first session's check, in its series driver (its as-run copy not published), was 'no listener on :4002 and no pgrep -f ibgateway match'. At 02:03 ET it matched another agent's Claude Code run whose command line carries that string; port 4002 had no listener and no Gateway process ran, so it was a false alarm, and the series stopped as its rule says. The pilots' checks with that test, before A1 and B1, left no log. The continuation used the owner's fixed check, which matches a listener on port 4002, executables under the Gateway's install folder and the process names java and ibgateway, never command lines. It reported 'gateway down' before each of B2, A2, A3 and B3 and after cleanup. Nothing connected to port 4002, and no trading lane or broker code ran.
deviations: Worktrees came from an unauthenticated scratch clone of the public repository, not meridian's main checkout (the main checkout must not change).

Probe count: 3 runs per arm, from the assessment, the earliest source ('3 runs each'), although method-dsh ('one probe call per arm (n=0)'), the fact sheet ('n=0 probe per arm') and method-dsh's check ('run the n=0 probe on the task base'), all later, say one probe per arm. The precedence 'the later file wins' is stated only in the published pre-registration, written after the runs; no source written before them sets it. Found afterwards.
The probe worktrees had no uv sync (the prompt does not read .venv); the pilots set no TMPDIR. The probe does not need either: the captures are identical with and without TMPDIR.
After the false stop the series continued one run per call with a new driver and the fixed check; the probe runner was unchanged.

The pilots A1 and B1, made with an earlier, unkept probe runner, were counted as runs a1 and b1 of the 3+3, although the first driver had planned six fresh runs after them; so 2 runs per arm come from the published runner. The counts are unaffected: every run of an arm is byte-identical in system text, tools and request options.

Pilot A1 (02:00:58 to 02:01:00 ET) ran about 15 s before the pre-registered dump, diff and stop check (dumps 02:01:15 ET); the profile init files (01:56:58 ET) lack the overlay rows. B1 and the continuation runs came after the check. A1 ran inside bwrap --unshare-net, so nothing could be uploaded, and it is byte-identical to A2 and A3.

The pre-registration's 'overlay last in both arms' held only in arm A: in arm B the with-only patch came after the overlay (as ab-dsh.md's own run line has it). That row only inserts goal-gate and changes no overlay row.

Run order a1 b1 b2 a2 a3 b3 from the fact sheet and ab-tasks.md, although method-dsh's check, the later file, gives b1 a1 a2 b2 b3 a3. The precedence 'the later file wins' is stated only in the published pre-registration, written after the runs; no source written before them sets it. Found afterwards.
cost: DeepSeek tokens billed: 0. No request left the machine: every dsh run, profile init and dump ran in bwrap --unshare-net, the runs against a 127.0.0.1 capture endpoint with the placeholder key 'capture-only-placeholder'; the owner's key was never read, sourced, copied or linked. Claude Code agents started 0, Codex runs 0; dsh sessions 6, the probe runs, none reaching a model (plus the profile inits and dumps). This measurement made 0 GitHub REST and 0 GraphQL calls (only unauthenticated git clones, all removed); the re-check it relies on made 5 REST and 2 GraphQL calls.
containment: Per run: see runs. Over both sessions: the owner's five dsh files hash-identical before and after (sha256sum -c OK), nothing under ~/.dsh newer than the start stamps, the home folder's top level unchanged, nothing run against meridian's main checkout (read-only worktree lists with --no-optional-locks only). Apart from the pilots' spill roots in /tmp (dsh's own, in both arms, because the pilots set no TMPDIR; see runs A1 and B1), changes in /tmp and in the main checkout's worktree list during the sessions came from other agents' measurements, between runs; each continuation run's own diffs are 0.
